descriptionChirho: A high-quality white linen fabric (byssus), used for priestly garments, temple curtains, and royal clothing in Chronicles and Ezekiel. All three clusters represent the same material noun with purely grammatical differences: bare noun (fine linen), with conjunction and preposition (and in the fine linen), and with the definite article (the linen). Cross-linguistically uniform: Spanish lino fino, Arabic كَتَّان (kattan) / بُوص (bus), Korean 세마포 (semapo), Swahili kitani, Hindi सन (san) all consistently denote fine woven linen cloth, confirming a single lexical sense.
